what: WORKED COMPUTATION (independent run 1 of 2): Which pasts give a Newtonian kernel. For the linear gain-one formation model on a 3+1 event lattice whose record at (t+1, x) averages the records at (t, x + p), p in a finite set P, the equal-time kernel is sigma^2/(1 - |phi|^2), phi(k) = |P|^-1 sum_p e^{ik.p}. For P = (a) the site and its 6 neighbours, (b) the 6 neighbours only, (c) site + 6 + 12 face diagonals, (d) the 8 cube corners, (e) the backward set {0, e1, e2, e3}, (f) the site and 3 backward + 3 forward neighbours chosen asymmetrically: compute with sympy the small-k form 1 - |phi|^2 = k^T M k + ..., whether M is isotropic, the drift (the imaginary linear term of phi), and ALL zeros of 1 - |phi|^2 on the Brillouin zone (a zero away from k = 0 is a second massless mode, a doubler: expected for (b) and (d) at k = (pi,pi,pi), since phi = -1 there). Table: set, isotropic?, drift?, doublers?, the bounded factor relating the kernel to 1/E(k). Expectation: cube-symmetric sets containing the site itself give an isotropic, drift-free, doubler-free Green-function kernel. DELIVERABLE in your unit worktree: probes/work/compute/kernel-by-predecessor-set/<your worker name>/run.py (self-contained; exact arithmetic wherever the statement is exact; numpy only for the numerical cross-checks named) and RESULT.md (the table or formulas, in plain text). run.py prints one line per result, a final `SUMMARY: <the main result in one line>`, and `HIT: <what>` ONLY if a result contradicts the expectation stated in the task (that is the interesting case: report it precisely). Two workers do each computation independently; the supervisor compares them. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/compute/kernel-by-predecessor-set/<name>/run.py"
